canon_summary: The protagonist is Lina (莉娜), a curious girl in a red coat. Mosk (莫斯克) is a grumpy grey old fox in a green vest guarding a humming tree. Lina gives Mosk an apple. The tree hums because a firefly queen is inside; long ago Mosk failed to save a friend with medicine. These later reveals (firefly/queen/medicine) are SPOILERS for early scenes.

scenes.text: On the edge of the little wool-grey village where Lina lived, there stood a hollow tree taller than the church. Every winter night, a low humming drifted out of its bark, and the grown-ups said: leave that tree alone. But the night her grandmother fell asleep without finishing their story, Lina put on her red wool coat and walked across the frosty field to listen.

Inside the hollow tree she found a curl of stairs going down, and at the very top step sat an old grey fox in a patched green vest. His name was Mosk. He told her, in a voice like dry leaves, that the tree was not for visiting and that she should go home and forget the humming. Lina said she could not forget what she had not yet heard.

Mosk pointed at the door. Lina reached into her pocket and pulled out the last apple of the season. She set it on the step between them and said, this is for the trouble of walking me down. Mosk stared at the apple for a long time. Then he stood up, tied his vest, and stepped onto the first stair without a word.

At the bottom of the stairs the humming was a quiet song, and a firefly the size of a robin lay on a bed of moss. Her glow was almost out. Mosk's whiskers trembled. She had been his friend once, he whispered, and one winter long ago he had failed to bring her medicine in time. He had been guarding the tree ever since, ashamed to face her.

Lina knelt and asked the firefly queen what she needed. A drop of warm milk and a kind word, said the queen, that was all medicine ever was. Mosk fetched the milk in a thimble and laid his paw beside hers. The queen's glow steadied. The humming inside the tree turned into a tune Lina had not heard before — and Mosk, for the first time in years, hummed along.
